intent: The primitive's portal, which moves what it holds out of the page's DOM tree into the document body or a given container while its Drawer is mounted.
typical_uses: A layer a caller must portal beside the drawer's panel, outside it

dont_use_when.situation: Portalling the drawer's panel, or rendering it into a themed subtree

instead.note: DrawerContent portals itself; pass the subtree as its `container`.

invariants.text: The portal renders nothing while the drawer is closed and not animating closed, unless `keepMounted` is set.
While the drawer is mounted and the root's `modal` is exactly `true`, the portal renders the primitive's transparent blocking backdrop before its children.

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the portal renders into; an explicit null renders nothing until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the portal's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.states: style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the portal's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit sets no style of its own on the portal.

good.title: A layer kept in the DOM while the drawer is closed

bad.title: The panel wrapped in a portal of its own
bad.why: DrawerContent already portals itself, so this nests a second portal and, while the drawer is modal, renders a second copy of the primitive's blocking backdrop.

container.description: TS: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the portal renders into; an explicit null renders nothing until a node is passed. `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, DrawerPortalState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the portal's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: DrawerPortalState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the portal's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit sets no style of its own on the portal.
